subject: Biochemistry
title: Lipoprotein Metabolism & Familial Dyslipidemias
preview: Lipoprotein metabolism is easier when each apoprotein is linked to its key transport role.

sections.title: Key apoproteins at a glance
points: ApoB-48: chylomicron structure and intestinal lipoprotein assembly.
ApoB-100: hepatic VLDL/LDL structural protein and LDL receptor interaction.
ApoC-II: activator of lipoprotein lipase; ApoE: hepatic remnant uptake; ApoA-I: HDL structure and LCAT activation.

sections.title: Different genetic patterns
points: Familial chylomicronemia impairs clearance of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and can cause recurrent pancreatitis.
Familial hypercholesterolemia commonly involves LDL receptor pathway defects with accelerated atherosclerosis and tendon xanthomas.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Severe triglyceride elevation is not interchangeable with isolated LDL elevation.
A normal total cholesterol result does not exclude every inherited lipoprotein disorder.

quickRevision: ApoB-48 is associated with intestinal chylomicrons; ApoB-100 supports LDL receptor binding.
ApoC-II supports lipoprotein lipase, while ApoE helps remnant clearance.
Very high triglycerides can raise pancreatitis risk, whereas LDL-associated disorders chiefly affect atherosclerotic risk.

quiz.question: Familial hypercholesterolemia commonly involves impaired handling of what?
quiz.explanation: LDL particles. Familial hypercholesterolemia commonly involves LDL receptor pathway defects with accelerated atherosclerosis and tendon xanthomas.
